steps.title: Import React
steps.instruction: Import React from the 'react' package to use JSX and create components.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring React into your file. This is required for any React component.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing a library
import React from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have React imported and ready to use for building components.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React. This allows you to use JSX and create React components.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're importing React from the 'react' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to import React from 'react' to use React features.

steps.title: Create the main App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns an empty div element.
steps.hint: Define a function called App that returns JSX containing a <div> tag.
steps.seedCode:
// Import React here

// Create the App component here
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is defined and returns an empty div.
successCriteria: A functional component named App exists and returns a <div> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the App component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined a component named App that returns a <div>.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component isn't defined correctly. Create a function named App that returns a <div> element.

steps.expectedOutcome: The Parent component is defined and ready to receive props.

steps.title: Create a Child component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named Child that accepts props and returns an empty div.
steps.hint: Define a new component function called Child that takes props as a parameter and returns JSX.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a Child component that can receive props from its parent.
successCriteria: A Child component is defined, accepts props, and returns an empty div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the Child component, which will be part of the props drilling chain.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component is named Child, accepts props, and returns a div element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Child component is not correctly defined. Check the component name, props parameter, and return statement.

steps.title: Create a Grandchild component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named Grandchild that accepts props and returns an empty div element.
steps.hint: Define a new component function that takes props as a parameter and returns JSX with a div.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Grandchild component is defined, ready to receive props through drilling.
successCriteria: Grandchild component is created as a function that accepts props and returns a div.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the Grandchild component. This will be the deepest component that receives props through drilling.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component is named Grandchild, accepts props, and returns a div element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't quite right. Check that you've defined a function named Grandchild that takes props and returns a div.

steps.title: Add data to App component
steps.instruction: Inside the App component, create a constant variable named 'userData' with properties for name and age (e.g., name: 'Alex', age: 25).
steps.hint: Define a const variable inside the App component's function body, before the return statement.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component now contains a userData object with name and age properties, ready to be passed down through props.
successCriteria: A constant variable named 'userData' is defined inside the App component with at least 'name' and 'age' properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the user data at the top level. This data will be passed down through the component hierarchy.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure 'userData' is a constant variable defined inside the App component with both 'name' and 'age' properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Create a constant variable named 'userData' inside the App component with properties like name and age.

steps.title: Pass data from App to Parent
steps.instruction: Inside the App component's return statement, render the Parent component and pass the userData constant as a prop named 'data'.
steps.hint: Add <Parent data={userData} /> inside the div after the heading.
steps.analogousExample:
// Passing a prop to a component
<ComponentName propName={value} />
steps.expectedOutcome: The Parent component will be rendered inside App and receive the userData as a prop, starting the props drilling chain.
successCriteria: Parent component is rendered in App's return with a prop named 'data' whose value is userData.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully passed the data from App to Parent as a prop. This is the first step in props drilling.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're rendering the Parent component and passing userData as a prop named 'data'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to render the Parent component inside App and pass userData as a prop called 'data'.

steps.title: Pass data from Parent to Child
steps.instruction: Inside the Parent component, render the Child component and pass the 'data' prop you receive from App as a prop to Child.
steps.hint: In the Parent component's return statement, add the Child component with a prop like data={data}.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Parent component will render the Child component and pass the data prop through to it.
successCriteria: Child component is rendered inside Parent's return statement with a data prop passed to it.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully passed the data prop from Parent to Child, demonstrating props drilling through an intermediate component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're rendering the Child component inside Parent and passing the data prop to it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Child component isn't being rendered or the data prop isn't being passed correctly. Check that you're passing the data prop from Parent to Child.

steps.title: Pass data from Child to Grandchild
steps.instruction: Inside the Child component, render the Grandchild component and pass the 'data' prop you receive from Parent down to Grandchild as a prop.
steps.hint: Add <Grandchild data={data} /> inside the return statement of the Child component.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Child component will render the Grandchild component and pass the 'data' prop through, completing the props drilling chain from App to Grandchild.
successCriteria: The Child component renders the Grandchild component with a 'data' prop passed to it.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully passed the data prop from Child to Grandchild, completing the props drilling chain.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're rendering the Grandchild component and passing the 'data' prop to it inside the Child component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Child component should render the Grandchild component and pass the 'data' prop to it. Check that you've added <Grandchild data={data} /> inside the Child's return statement.

steps.title: Display data in Grandchild
steps.instruction: In the Grandchild component, display the 'data' prop values (like name and age) in the JSX by adding them inside the existing <div>.
steps.hint: Access the prop values using props.data.name and props.data.age, then render them in JSX.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Grandchild component will show the name and age values passed through props from the App component.
successCriteria: The Grandchild component renders the name and age values from props.data in its JSX.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully displayed the drilled props in the deepest component, completing the props drilling chain.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're accessing props.data.name and props.data.age and rendering them inside the JSX.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Grandchild component should display the name and age values from the data prop. Check that you're using props.data.name and props.data.age in the JSX.
